candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — environmental cleaning monitoring / ATP bioluminescence
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret ATP bioluminescence as an objective indicator of residual organic material used to assess environmental cleaning effectiveness, not as a pathogen-identification or sterility test.

options.A: An objective indicator of residual organic material that can help assess cleaning effectiveness
options.B: Identification of the exact pathogen species present on the surface
options.C: Confirmation that the surface is sterile after cleaning
options.D: A measurement that replaces the need to perform environmental cleaning

candidate.rationale: CDC guidance states that ATP bioluminescence detects ATP as an indicator that organic microbial or biologic material is present on a surface. Comparing measurements before and after cleaning can provide objective feedback about cleaning effectiveness. ATP testing does not identify a specific pathogen, does not establish sterility, and does not replace cleaning. CDC also notes limitations including low sensitivity/specificity and lack of a standardized threshold for declaring a surface 'safe.'
candidate.source_claim_supported: ATP bioluminescence detects residual organic material and can provide objective before/after information about cleaning effectiveness, but it does not identify specific pathogens or establish sterility.
